teams.heading: Former England international set to make Fiji Test debut against France
teams.body: Fiji's next assignment is at Groupama Stadium in Lyon, where Jake White's side face France on Saturday. Reports say a former England international is set to win a first Fiji cap in the match. It is Fiji's fourth Nations Championship game: the three July defeats, including 39-24 to Wales and 73-8 to England, came under interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula, before White was appointed.

teams.heading: George Furbank recalled at full-back as Borthwick names England side for Australia
teams.body: Fin Smith has been declared fit after an injury scare in the build-up, and Planet Rugby reports he has started England's past five matches at fly-half. George Furbank is back on the team sheet at full-back, having been kept out of the Test side since November 2024 by injuries and an appendicitis bout in the July window; the report calls him in strong form at Harlequins. Greg Fisilau is in the matchday squad and in line for a maiden Test cap.

lead.why: A fresh England team announcement with a headline return at full-back and a debutant in the matchday squad.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié names uncapped Esteban Capilla in France's matchday 23 against Fiji
teams.body: Esteban Capilla was named in France's matchday 23 for Saturday's France v Fiji in Lyon, and RTÉ Sport reports he could make his debut off the bench. He earned his place after Oscar Jegou was injured on Wednesday. Antoine Dupont captains the side from scrum-half, partnering Romain Ntamack at half-back, while Louis Bielle-Biarrey starts on the wing.

teams.heading: Captain Dan Sheehan forced off after failed head assessment against Argentina
teams.body: Against Argentina on Friday night, Dan Sheehan was forced off in the first half after failing a head injury assessment, and head coach Andy Farrell said the captain "seems fine in the dressing room". Robert Baloucoune also went off with a knock in the 58th minute, while Sean Jansen sustained a "bang" to his knee. Josh van der Flier and Mack Hansen both have ankle concerns, with Hansen continuing after treatment.

teams.heading: Quesada names kicking game among what failed in Springboks defeat
teams.body: Speaking after the 66-7 defeat in Turin, head coach Gonzalo Quesada called the Springboks' first half one of the best recently, but was candid about Italy's own failings: the kicking game and clearance kicks did not work, and in some situations they put themselves under pressure. He pointed to positives, including defence against the driving maul and a partial second-half comeback until the 70th minute, when Italy had more ball. Captain Giacomo Nicotera said he was disappointed that Italy had not fully respected their values.

teams.heading: Sione Tuipulotu takes full responsibility for Scotland's second-half collapse against New Zealand
teams.body: Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu has put the blame on himself for the 43-21 defeat, saying the side were "nowhere near accurate enough" in the second half. Tuipulotu was sin-binned on 50 minutes as Scotland conceded 13 penalties to New Zealand's eight, and New Zealand scored three tries after the interval without reply. "Our discipline wasn't good enough, and it starts with me," he said, adding that Scotland now face a "must-win game" against Australia next week.

teams.heading: Rees-Zammit ends eight-Test tryless run in Wales' 28-21 win over Japan
teams.body: Louis Rees-Zammit stepped over just before half-time, after Eddie James had created the space, ending an eight-Test run without a try. Tomos Williams then released Josh Adams for his second, and Wales were made to sweat when Japan's Shinya Komura scored four minutes from time to cut the gap to a single score. Steve Tandy's side still took the bonus point for a second win of the tournament.

teams.heading: Justo Piccardo and Efraín Elías yellow-carded in Dublin defeat to Ireland
teams.body: Justo Piccardo was sin-binned for offside on 34 minutes while defending near the try zone, leaving Argentina a man short, and Efraín Elías followed for a high tackle on Hugo Keenan later in the match. Rónan Kelleher's lineout maul for Ireland's sixth try came against a seven-man Pumas pack. The cards compounded the loss of captain Julián Montoya, who failed a head injury assessment before half-time and did not return.

teams.heading: Fraser McReight 50th cap; Jeremy Williams starts at blindside against England
teams.body: Fraser McReight will earn his 50th cap on Sunday, with Jeremy Williams picked at blindside flanker and Harry Wilson captaining from number eight. Len Ikitau returns to midfield after missing the last Test under HIA protocols, alongside Isaac Henry, who starts his first Test in the United Kingdom. Tom Wright starts at full-back for the 10th straight Test, and Taniela Tupou is back on the bench.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones starts uncapped Riku Kitahara at fly-half against Wales in Cardiff
teams.body: Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee are injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who started all of Japan's Tests this year, is back at university and misses the whole tour. Eddie Jones opted to start Honda Heat's uncapped Riku Kitahara at fly-half, with Toyota's Shinya Komura, who won his last of three caps against Georgia in November 2025, on the bench as the only other option. Japan lost 21-28 to Wales in Cardiff on Saturday.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett's brace helps All Blacks beat Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield
teams.body: New Zealand scored seven tries in a 43-21 win over Scotland at Murrayfield on Saturday, and the second half decided it. Only three points separated the teams at the break, but Scotland failed to score after it, while Josh Moorby, Beauden Barrett (two tries) and Asafo Aumua crossed for the visitors. Ewan Ashman's first-half hat-trick for Scotland was not enough. Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi both went to the sin-bin in the first half.

teams.heading: Salmaan Moerat withdrawn from Springbok XV with back spasms before Turin
teams.body: Head coach Rassie Erasmus confirmed that Salmaan Moerat, set to make his first Test appearance of 2026, withdrew late from the starting XV, with Lood de Jager promoted and Franco Mostert named on the bench. Moerat had a niggle on Thursday and picked up more back spasms in the warm-up. "Salmaan's got back spasms," Erasmus said after the 66-7 win, and he described Moerat as the only casualty of the game, with no other serious injuries reported. The Boks now prepare for France in Paris.

lead.why: A fresh team-news item on a late Springbok withdrawal, which is more newsworthy than the match report or post-match quotes already covered.
